issues.failure_explanation: Every convergence result of the paper (Proposition prop:thetarange, Lemma lem:monotonic, Theorem thm:conv, Theorem convergerate) requires T to be alpha-averaged nonexpansive with alpha in (0,1/2]. The restriction is essential to the method: T^{theta_k} = (1-alpha(1+theta_k))I + alpha(1+theta_k)N with theta_k as large as 1 (Proposition prop:thetarange(i)) is nonexpansive in general only when 2*alpha <= 1; otherwise T^{theta_k} can be expansive and the Fejer-type descent in Lemma lem:monotonic (and hence Theorem thm:conv and the rate in Theorem convergerate) breaks down. In the numerical section the paper verifies only plain averaged nonexpansiveness of the TV-denoising operator T_2 (lambda<1/4) and of the projected-gradient operator T_3 (step alpha<2/L), with no averagedness constant, and then applies TKMA as if the theory covered them. Standard composition bounds for such prox-of-affine / projected-gradient compositions certify only constants larger than 1/2, and with the parameters actually used the hypothesis is provably violated: for T_3 with L=1 and step alpha=1.99, on any neighborhood where the projection onto the nuclear-norm ball is inactive (e.g. around X* = (1.99/0.99) P_Omega A, which is mapped to 0 in the interior of the constraint set), T_3 coincides with the affine map X -> P_{Omega^c}X - 0.99 P_Omega X + 1.99 P_Omega A; inserting pairs differing along Omega-supported directions into the averagedness inequality (Lemma lem:equivAN) forces every averagedness constant of T_3 to be at least 3.9601/3.98 ≈ 0.995 > 1/2. Hence Theorem thm:conv and Theorem convergerate do not apply to the matrix-completion experiment as stated, and the same unverified (generically violated) hypothesis applies to the TV-denoising operator, whose affine part I - lambda B B^T has eigenvalues near -0.999 for lambda = 0.999/4.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (i) extend the convergence analysis to alpha-averaged operators with alpha in (1/2,1), which requires genuinely new arguments because Proposition prop:thetarange(ii) and the descent in Lemma lem:monotonic fail there (T^{theta_k} may be expansive and theta_k may be negative); or (ii) restrict the experiments to operators certified alpha<=1/2-averaged, which excludes the showcased parameter regimes (standard composition bounds for these projected-gradient/prox-affine operators in dimension >= 2 certify only constants > 1/2); or (iii) explicitly state that the experiments run outside the proven regime and are supported only empirically, withdrawing the implied guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The proved convergence (Theorem thm:conv) and the o(1/sqrt(k)) rate (Theorem convergerate) do not provably cover the two showcased applications with the stated parameters; the advertised theoretically guaranteed applicability of TKMA to TV image denoising and low-rank matrix completion (title, abstract, contribution (iii), and the two TKMA pseudocode blocks) is unsupported, and for the matrix-completion setup with step size 1.99 it is false. The formal results themselves remain valid for the class of alpha-averaged operators with alpha in (0,1/2].
issues.title: Application operators in the experiments are not certified (and for matrix completion provably are not) alpha<=1/2-averaged as required by TKMA's convergence theory
issues.why_classification: All formal results remain correct as stated and cover the nonempty class of alpha<=1/2-averaged (in particular all firmly nonexpansive) operators; only the unlabeled applicability claims linking the theory to the two experiments fail. A limited weakening that scopes those claims honestly (resolution (iii)), or a contained new analysis extending the theory, preserves every theorem, the algorithm, and the numerical evidence, so a recognizably comparable paper survives without rebuilding the existing proofs; but the repair is beyond a routine local fix since the hypothesis is provably violated for the showcased matrix-completion parameters.
